correctness.rationale: In real orthogonal Schur coordinates the drift is A=[[-a-b,h],[0,-a+b]]. The stationary Lyapunov equation forces D=B/2=-(A+A^T)/2 and tr B=4a. The diffusion eigenvalues are a±c with c=sqrt(b^2+h^2/4); strict positivity requires c<a. Every b<=c<a occurs, with spectrum unchanged, and stability and the Lyapunov equation give the same N(0,I). The current matrix W=A+D is skew with magnitude |h|/2, hence Phi=tr(W^T D^(-1) W)=2a(c^2-b^2)/(a^2-c^2). Substitution of c=a(K-1)/(K+1) proves the claimed curve. Phi'=(a^2-b^2)(1-K^(-2))/(2a)>0 on the feasible domain, so a feasible finite cap is attained at its upper endpoint. From C(tau)=exp(A^T tau), the off-diagonal lag difference has magnitude |h|e^(-a tau)sinh(b tau)/b, giving the stated Frobenius norm and its limiting bound. The boundary c=a is not in the model class. For tau>0 the lag supremum is approached and not attained; tau=0 is identically zero. The saturation is not non-identifiability from exact positive-lag norm data at fixed a,b, since that norm is strictly increasing in c.
residual_risks: The classification uses Euclidean conditioning at identity stationary covariance and the physical diffusion tensor B/2. It does not assign EPR to singular noise or establish an estimation error bound.

evidence: Troude–Sornette permit general correlated positive-definite forcing for exactly this stable real-spectrum drift. The forced B=-(A+A^T) is their equal-variance case sigma_i^2=2a, correlation rho=-c/a. Their effective nonnormality K_sigma=(kappa-kappa^(-1))/2=v/b.

Godrèche–Luck give a general planar EPR identity. Nagayama et al.'s relaxation-speedup lower bound is weaker on this class, 2(c-b)^2/(a+c), and is not itself the exact frontier. The other cited formulas are general linear diffusion identities.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The broader correlated-forcing formulas actually evaluate the whole constrained family. It is this direct specialization of an already-solved parametrized problem, not generic availability of OU tools, that gives coverage.

evidence: With c=b(kappa+kappa^(-1))/2 and v=b(kappa-kappa^(-1))/2, c ranges from b to a under B>0, with a excluded. Eq. (12) gives exactly 2a(c^2-b^2)/(a^2-c^2). The eigenvalues 2(a±c) of the forced Eq. (9) give K=(a+c)/(a-c); the claimed eliminated Phi(K), feasible K-range and capped maximum follow directly.

The propagator from Eqs. (50)–(51) and identity covariance give |C12-C21|=(v/b)|e^(-(a-b)tau)-e^(-(a+b)tau)|. This agrees with Eqs. (57)–(58) for the norm of (C-C^T)/2, so the frozen full-difference norm is twice that quantity. Eq. (8) in the main text uses a different factor; the comparison uses the matrix propagator and the consistent supplement convention. The finite lag limit and divergent EPR are the c↑a limit of those formulas.

evidence: Subtract the trace and decompose A+aI into symmetric traceless S and skew W. Rotate the ±c eigenbasis of S so S has zero diagonal and off-diagonal c; swapping axes if needed preserves S while choosing W's upper entry v>=0. The resulting drift has off-diagonals c+v and c-v, with (c+v)(c-v)=b^2 and c>v. Thus it is exactly Eq. (3) with alpha=a, beta=b and kappa=(c+v)/b>=1.
Orthogonal changes preserve identity covariance, diffusion eigenvalues, entropy production and the lag Frobenius norm, so this parametrization does not omit orientations or either circulation sign.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The previously solved parametrization exhausts the frozen class after stationarity is imposed; the apparent canonical-vs-all-orientations distinction does not leave a new feasible point. Troude–Sornette's drift nonnormality index is not the noise condition number.

originality.rationale: Troude–Sornette's earlier planar canonical drift and EPR/lag formulas already imply the complete frontier by stationary covariance matching and elimination, not just one example or a generic EPR identity. Every orientation of the frozen drift is orthogonally equivalent to their Eq. (3), and the required noise lies in their Eq. (9). Their Eq. (12) gives the exact rate, and the explicit propagator in §VI.2 gives the same finite-lag law. Eliminating the single drift parameter and observing monotonicity is mechanical. This is a claim-level implication, not an assertion that the prior paper expressly labels the eliminated quantity an anisotropy frontier.
residual_risks: The comparison makes no claim about earliest historical priority or that the exact eliminated formula is printed in the prior paper. The lag-normalization discrepancy is resolved by comparing the actual matrix quantity.
